channel.title: Increvio Guides
channel.description: Research-backed guides on staying consistent, nutrition and training.

item.title: How to Stay Consistent With Working Out (When Motivation Fades)
item.description: Motivation fades, systems don't. 9 research-backed ways to stay consistent with working out: plans, habits, friends, smaller wins and never missing twice.

item.title: How Long Does It Take to Form a Habit? (Not 21 Days)
item.description: The 21-day rule is a myth. Research says habits take 66 days on average, with a range of 18 to 254. Here's what that means for your workouts and diet.

item.title: How to Get Motivated to Work Out (and What to Do When You're Not)
item.description: No motivation to work out? 10 research-backed ways to get yourself to the gym, plus why waiting for motivation is the wrong strategy in the first place.

item.title: Never Miss Twice: The Simple Rule That Saves Your Progress
item.description: Missing one workout doesn't hurt your progress. Missing two in a row starts a new habit. How the never-miss-twice rule works and how to use it.

item.title: Accountability Partner for Fitness: Why It Works and How to Find One
item.description: People who started with friends were far more likely to finish their program. How a fitness accountability partner works, who to pick, and how to set it up.

item.title: Why People Quit Working Out: 7 Reasons and How to Avoid Them
item.description: Most people who start working out quit within weeks. The 7 most common reasons, from all-or-nothing plans to invisible progress, and how to avoid each one.

item.title: When-Then Plans: The Easiest Way to Actually Do Your Workouts
item.description: Writing down when and where you'll exercise raised follow-through to 91% in one study. How to make when-then plans for training and food.

item.title: How to Get Back on Track After Falling Off Your Fitness Routine
item.description: Fell off your workout or diet routine? How to restart without guilt, how much strength you actually lost, and a simple 2-week plan to get back on track.

item.title: Do Fitness Streaks Work? How to Use Streaks Without Burning Out
item.description: Streaks can make habits stick, but a broken streak can make people quit. What research says about streaks and how to design one that keeps you going.

item.title: How to Stick to a Diet: 10 Strategies That Actually Work
item.description: The best diet is the one you can stick to. 10 research-backed strategies to stay on track with healthy eating, from meal planning to the 80/20 rule.

item.title: How Much Protein Per Day? The Research-Backed Answer
item.description: How much protein do you need per day to build muscle or lose fat? Research says 1.6 to 2.2 g per kg. Tables by body weight, timing and food examples.

item.title: How Many Calories to Build Muscle? Lean Bulk Without Getting Fat
item.description: You need a small calorie surplus to build muscle, not a big one. How to calculate your calories, how fast to gain, and why a lean bulk beats dirty bulking.

item.title: How Fast Should You Lose Weight? A Safe, Realistic Pace
item.description: Aim to lose about 0.5 to 1% of your body weight per week. Why slower fat loss protects muscle, how to set your deficit, and what to expect month by month.

item.title: Meal Prep for Beginners: A Simple Sunday System
item.description: Meal prep for beginners, step by step. How to plan, shop and cook a week of healthy meals in about 2 hours, with a sample plan, storage times and tips.

item.title: How to Make a Weekly Meal Plan and Grocery List (Template)
item.description: How to build a healthy weekly meal plan and a grocery list sorted by aisle in 20 minutes. Step-by-step method, example week and tips to save time and money.

item.title: Eating Out on a Diet: How to Enjoy Restaurants Without Losing Progress
item.description: You don't have to skip restaurants to lose fat or build muscle. What to order when eating out on a diet and how to adjust your day.

item.title: Weight Loss Plateau: Why It Happens and How to Break It
item.description: Stuck on a weight loss plateau? Why progress slows down, how to tell a real plateau from water weight, and 6 research-backed ways to get moving again.

item.title: Creatine: What It Does, How Much to Take and Is It Safe?
item.description: The most researched supplement for strength and muscle. What creatine does, how much to take (3 to 5 g a day), timing and safety.

item.title: How to Start Working Out: A Beginner's Guide That Sticks
item.description: New to working out? How to start strength training as a beginner: how often, which exercises, how heavy, a simple 3-day plan, and how to make it stick.

item.title: How Many Sets Per Week to Build Muscle? The Research Answer
item.description: Aim for at least 10 hard sets per muscle per week to build muscle. What the research says about training volume, how to count sets and how to split them.

item.title: Progressive Overload Explained: How to Keep Getting Stronger
item.description: Progressive overload is how you keep building muscle and strength. What it is, why it works, and the double progression method that makes it simple.

item.title: How Many Days a Week Should You Work Out?
item.description: How many days a week should you work out to build muscle or lose fat? Research-backed answers for 2, 3, 4 and 5 days, with example splits for each.

item.title: No Time to Work Out? How to Train Effectively in 20 to 30 Minutes
item.description: No time for the gym? How to build muscle and stay consistent with short 20 to 30 minute workouts, using supersets, smart exercise choice and fewer warm-up sets.

item.title: How Close to Failure Should You Train to Build Muscle?
item.description: Do you need to train to failure to build muscle? Research says stopping 1 to 2 reps short works about as well, with less fatigue. How to judge reps in reserve.

item.title: Cardio or Weights for Fat Loss? Why You Need Both
item.description: Cardio or weights for fat loss? Diet drives fat loss, weights protect muscle, cardio adds burn. How to combine them without losing gains.
